title: Bonjour ! Introducing yourself
description: Greet people, introduce yourself and choose between tu and vous: your first minute of French on a visit to ITER in Provence.

sources.title: ITER (Wikipedia)
sources.note: Built near the Cadarache research centre in southern France; headquarters Saint-Paul-lez-Durance; seven members: China, the EU, India, Japan, Korea, Russia, the United States.

sources.title: ITER Organization: Visiting ITER
sources.note: Visitor Centre with a belvedere over the platform; the site is about 35 km north of Aix-en-Provence; group visits booked weeks ahead; visitors at least 16 years old, under-18s with a parent or guardian.

sources.title: Saint-Paul-lez-Durance (Wikipédia)
sources.note: Commune in Bouches-du-Rhône, Provence-Alpes-Côte d'Azur, home of the Cadarache centre and ITER.

sources.title: Tutoiement et vouvoiement en français (Wikipédia)
sources.note: Vous with strangers, tu among young people; moving from vous to tu is common, back is rare; tu is frequent in scientific and technical work.

sources.title: salut (Wiktionnaire)
sources.note: Familiar greeting, both hello and goodbye.

sources.title: bonsoir (Wiktionnaire)
sources.note: Evening greeting, when meeting and when leaving.

sources.title: Liaison (French) (Wikipedia)
sources.note: Liaison between a subject pronoun and the verb is obligatory; silent final consonants.

sources.title: French phonology (Wikipedia)
sources.note: The uvular r; the nasal vowels.
